pr_title: mac: always pass a non-NULL output size pointer to providers.
pr_body:
The backend code varies for the different MACs and sometimes sets the output
length, sometimes checks the return pointer and sometimes neither/either.

Fixes #12425
pr_comments: Should this change update the commit to run the external tests?

> Should this change update the commit to run the external tests?

To what purpose?

> To what purpose?

I was under the assumption that EVP_MAC_final is called by a few things (including apps) that could be affected by the change..
This pull request is ready to merge

issue_context.title: EVP_MAC_final segfault on NULL outl
issue_context.body:
Hello,

while playing with the EVP_MAC API I noticed, that ``EVP_MAC_final`` sometimes crashed with a NULL reference if ``outl`` was NULL.

While looking into this I noticed, that everything is fine and as documented in ``mac_lib.c``:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/crypto/evp/mac_lib.c#L120-L132

But the provider implementations work very different:

**Blake2, CMAC and poly1305 don't set it at all:**
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/providers/implementations/macs/blake2_mac_impl.c#L98-L105

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/providers/implementations/macs/cmac_prov.c#L116-L122

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/providers/implementations/macs/poly1305_prov.c#L91-L98

**GMAC and Siphash set it without a NULL check:**
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/providers/implementations/macs/gmac_prov.c#L111-L128

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/providers/implementations/macs/siphash_prov.c#L98-L109

**HMAC sets it with a NULL check:**
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/providers/implementations/macs/hmac_prov.c#L125-L136

**KMAC only sets it if the operation was ok:**
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a01cae99ac384cb6a74b46ccdc90736fe0754958/providers/implementations/macs/kmac_prov.c#L286-L304

So my first question would be, what is the expected correct behaviour? Who is resposible for setting this value?

If it is ``EVP_MAC_final`` is would suggest removing the parameter from the provider implementations altogether.
comments:
@paulidale: Thank you for the fix, but what speeks against defining/demanding some specific behaviour for the MAC implementations?

Woulkd this not be better in the long run and avoid other problems?

I did consider updating the MACs to be consistent, but decided having the framework do more was a safer  approach.  The framework supplies a default size, an individual MAC can replace this if it want.  This seems less error prone than insisting each MAC does all of this.  I guess it comes down to personal preference.

I didn't remove the NULL checks from those MACs that did do them and arguably should have.

Hmm, I'm still not convinced, that the entire procedure is necessary.
If the MAC returns something different than reported by ``EVP_MAC_size(ctx)`` I would consider this a violation of API.

And if we could agree on this, the ``outl`` parameter could be removed from the provider implementations entirely and thus removing the problem at its root.

I had a brief discussion with some of the other team members and the consensus was keeping the `outl` parameter wasn't harmful and helps with future proofing.  If someone doesn't want to bother with it, pass NULL and it will be ignored.

review_comments: It looks like EVP_MAC_size() cant be negative now - so this removal should be ok..
It returns a _size_t_ so could never be negative.  It was being assigned into an _int_ and the negative check was for overflow.  This cannot happen now since the assignment is now to a _size_t_.
